sample_unit: simulated triages (391 vignettes x 9 prompts x 10 repetitions)

links.outcome: Repeatability and reproducibility of LLM triage outputs across repeated runs and paraphrased prompts
links.effect: Repeatability was 14% of overall variation; reproducibility was 4.1%. Accuracy varied by prompt from 46.7% to 71.8%.
links.quote: Repeatability (use of the same prompt repeatedly) was 14% of the overall variation.

links.outcome: Accuracy of commercial LLM for START disaster triage against specialist reference standard
links.effect: Accuracy was 63.9% with 32.9% overtriage and 3.1% undertriage; conclusion that ChatGPT-4 is insufficient for START triage.
links.quote: The accuracy of ChatGPT for START was 63.9% with a 32.9% overtriage rate and a 3.1% undertriage rate.

unlisted_practices: Gage repeatability and reproducibility (gage R&R) statistical evaluation of LLM tools before clinical implementation

screen.reason: The study evaluates the accuracy, repeatability, and reproducibility of ChatGPT-4 on simulated disaster triage vignettes across different prompts, but does not compare or evaluate a specific organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
